_comment: THE ROOTWAYS (player-facing name, WO-1044 R1/R2, owner 2026-08-17; origin = the Heart's own roots, which is WHY the tunnel is quiet -- the song runs down here, so the rot does not). THE GRAPH ID STAYS 'dg_hollow_roads' ON PURPOSE and is NOT to be renamed to match: it is a four-way contract with BiomeRoads.ArmRoomIdFor, this file's own name, HollowRoadsDropInjector and BiomeRoadsRegression, and it also keys the WO-1112 hero carry via HubScenes.IsComposedDungeon. Ids are live contracts; display names are not. The retired name 'The Hollow Roads' read as the HOLLOWED'S roads, promising enemies in a graph that authors none. -- the simple tunnel system between the castle hub and the four cardinal biomes (owner 2026-08-16: 'place a portal to simple tunnel system that will drop into the new biomes'). SIMPLE IS THE SPEC, NOT A HEDGE: nine rooms, no encounters, no traps, no keys, no locks, no oil stones, no chests. It is a CROSSROADS, not a dungeon -- the player walks in, picks a direction, and leaves. WHY TWO INTERSECTIONS AND NOT ONE: per Assets/Dungeon/Rooms/DEFAULT_ROOMS.md the kit's only 4-way is Intersection (N,E,S,W) and Straight carries S,N ONLY -- so a single Intersection entered from the south has just three free sockets and can carry three arms, not four. The second Intersection is the geometry's answer, not a flourish. ARM IDS ARE REGION NAMES, NOT COMPASS NAMES, on purpose: the tunnel's interior layout has no reason to agree with the world compass, and naming an arm 'arm_s' while it hangs off an east socket would be a comment that lies -- which is the exact failure CLAUDE.md's catalog rule exists for. The ids are the contract with DeNelle.Core.World.BiomeRoads.ArmRoomIdFor; renaming one here without renaming it there leaves a tunnel arm with no destination, and BiomeRoads fails loudly if that happens. Each arm's far end carries a BIOME DROP placed at runtime by HollowRoadsDropInjector, routing back out to Main_Castle_Overworld at a position DERIVED from measured terrain bounds. EGRESS: extracts is deliberately EMPTY. The four arms are OUTBOUND drops to the overworld, not extraction pads, and DungeonExitSpawner still injects exactly one front exit at exitRoomId ('entry' -- deliberately named 'entry' rather than 'mouth' so that the spawner's LAYOUT-LESS FALLBACK, which looks for a child literally named 'entry', lands on the right room even if the emitted layout JSON has not been mirrored into Resources yet) so the beacon count stays 1 and the way home is never in doubt. This graph id is NOT in DungeonEgressRegression.ContentLayouts or ControlGroupLayouts, so the [dungeon-egress] one-back-exit trim is neither tripped nor weakened -- a tunnel is a different KIND of space and is exempt by not being content, not by an assertion being loosened.
